instruction: Use Abaqus via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to perform a torsion analysis of a circular shaft (Variant A). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Part: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Revolution. Sketch in the X-Y plane a rectangle from (0, 0) to (5, 80). The left vertical edge at X = 0 serves as the revolution axis (global Y-axis). Revolve 360 deg to create a solid cylinder with diameter 10 mm and length 80 mm, aligned with the global Y-axis. Property: Create a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Solid Homogeneous section and assign it to the entire shaft. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the shaft. Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-Torque-A. Load: Apply an Encastre boundary condition to the fixed end face at Y = 0 (perpendicular to the Y-axis). Create a reference point RP-1 at the center of the free end face (Y = 80 mm) and couple it kinematically to that end face. Apply a torque (Moment) of 850 N*mm at RP-1 about the shaft axis (global Y-axis). Mesh: Apply a global seed size of 4 mm. Assign element type C3D8R and generate the mesh. Job: Create a job named Job-Torsion-A, submit it for analysis, and wait for successful completion. Save: Save the model database to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Torsion-A.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Torsion-A.odb. [Software] To start Abaqus/CAE, run `C:\SIMULIA\EstProducts\2023\win_b64\resources\install\cmdDirFeature\launcher.bat cae` (adjust path to your install).
